title: Why Garlic Breath Comes From Your Lungs the Next Morning & Why Tomato Juice Never De-Skunked Anyone — Suarez & Michael Levitt's Oral Methanethiol vs. >24-Hr Alveolar Allyl Methyl Sulfide (AMS) Gastric-Bypass Proof, Allium sativum PLP–Aminoacrylate C-S Lyase Catalysis Inside Garlic Alliinase (PDB 1LK9, 2HOX), Sheryl Barringer's SIFT-MS Raw-Apple Dicopper Polyphenol Oxidase (PDB 6ELS) & Mint Rosmarinic Acid Thiol Trapping, and Paul Kreiss's Alkaline Peroxide Skunk (E)-2-Butene-1-Thiol Sulfonation vs. 90-s CNGA2 Olfactory Adaptation

teenKit.tldr: Brushing your teeth won't stop next-day garlic breath because the sulfur compound AMS enters your bloodstream through your stomach and escapes directly out of your lungs hours later. Meanwhile, tomato juice won't fix a skunk-sprayed dog because old school tomato tricks are just nose fatigue, not chemical neutralization.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how volatile sulfur molecules bypass digestion and hijack your breath proves that our bodies are leaky chemical systems where surface hygiene can't outsmart internal biochemistry.
keyTakeaways: Garlic breath the next morning comes from your lungs exhaling Allyl Methyl Sulfide (AMS) absorbed through your digestive tract, meaning mouthwash never stands a chance.
Crushing raw garlic cells triggers an enzyme reaction that instantly converts harmless storage chemicals into pungent, tear-inducing defense vapors.
Raw apples and fresh mint can actually neutralize breath odors chemically if eaten at the right time because their natural compounds trap sulfur molecules before they hit your bloodstream.

vocab.name: Allyl Methyl Sulfide (AMS)
vocab.meaning: A stubborn sulfur molecule produced by digested garlic that enters your blood and gets exhaled by your lungs for over 24 hours.

vocab.name: Alliinase
vocab.meaning: An enzyme locked inside garlic cells that waits for a cell wall to break before instantly manufacturing pungent garlic odors.

vocab.name: Polyphenol Oxidase
vocab.meaning: An enzyme found in raw apples that reacts with oxygen to chemically trap and neutralize bad breath compounds.

vocab.name: Olfactory Adaptation
vocab.meaning: The scientific term for nose blindness, where your scent receptors simply quit registering a persistent smell after about 90 seconds.

quiz.question: Why does aggressive teeth brushing and mouthwash fail to cure morning-after garlic breath?
options: The bacteria live too deep in your throat for mouthwash to reach.
Garlic oils chemically bond permanently to tooth enamel overnight.
The odor molecules are exhaled from your lungs after being absorbed into your bloodstream.
Toothpaste reacts with garlic to create an even stronger odor.
quiz.explanation: Because AMS enters your bloodstream and travels to your lungs, brushing your teeth only cleans your mouth while your lungs keep continuously exhaling the gas.

quiz.question: What actually happens when a chef chops an unpeeled bulb of raw garlic?
options: Oxygen from the air bakes the garlic skin to release heat.
Cell walls rupture, allowing enzymes and stored compounds to mix and instantly create pungent sulfur vapor.
The garlic releases harmless water vapor to protect itself from drying out.
Natural sugars caramelize instantly upon touching the metal blade.
quiz.explanation: Chopping breaks physical cellular compartments, forcing the alliinase enzyme to react with alliin and produce the sharp sulfur compounds.

quiz.question: Why do people think tomato juice cures a skunk-sprayed dog when it actually doesn't?
options: Tomato acid completely destroys skunk thiol molecules on contact.
Skunk spray ingredients are completely soluble in tomato paste.
Olfactory adaptation causes human and dog nose receptors to get overwhelmed and temporarily stop registering the stench.
Tomato seeds absorb the liquid spray off the fur.
quiz.explanation: The intense scent overwhelms your nose receptors in under 90 seconds, making you falsely believe the tomato juice worked when the smell is actually still there.
